definitions.explanation: A cheap beer-flavoured drink made without malt (from peas or soy, for example) or from happōshu blended with spirits, so that it fell into a lower liquor-tax class than beer and happōshu. The name ranks it after real beer and low-malt beer. Tax reforms in 2023 and 2026 brought its tax up to beer's, but the name is still used for these drinks.

examples.japanese: {第三|だいさん}のビール⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}う→買う：00489_kau⟧。
⟦{節約|せつやく}→節約：03302_setsuyaku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ため→ため：01145_tame⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{第三|だいさん}のビール⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{切|き}り{替|か}えた→切り替える：04239_kirikaeru⟧。
examples.english: I switched to "third beer" to save money.

examples.japanese: ⟦{最近|さいきん}→最近：00881_saikin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{第三|だいさん}のビール⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{本物|ほんもの}→本物：03628_honmono⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ビール→ビール：01015_biiru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{区別|くべつ}→区別：01555_kubetsu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧つかないほどおいしい。
examples.english: Today's "third beers" taste so good you can hardly tell them from real beer.

notes:
Japanese supermarkets shelve three kinds of beer-like drink: ⟦ビール→ビール：01015_biiru⟧ (beer), ⟦{発泡酒|はっぽうしゅ}→発泡酒：33170_happoushu⟧ (low-malt beer) and {第三|だいさん}のビール. Makers created the third kind in the 2000s to sell a cheaper can by staying outside the higher tax classes.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {第三|だいさん}のビール⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{売|う}り{上|あ}げ: sales of third beer
- ⟦ビール→ビール：01015_biiru⟧、⟦{発泡酒|はっぽうしゅ}→発泡酒：33170_happoushu⟧、{第三|だいさん}のビール: beer, happōshu and third beer
- {酒税|しゅぜい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{改正|かいせい}→改正：00446_kaisei⟧: a liquor-tax revision

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {新|しん}⟦ジャンル→ジャンル：11017_janru⟧: "new genre"; the makers' own name for the same drinks
- ⟦{発泡酒|はっぽうしゅ}→発泡酒：33170_happoushu⟧: low-malt beer; contains some malt, taxed between beer and third beer
